incidents.vector: Active exploitation of an unpatched zero-day (CVE-2026-20245), an output-encoding flaw letting an authenticated or local attacker inject commands and execute as root, often chained with earlier Cisco SD-WAN zero-days for the required access.
incidents.impact: Seventh actively exploited Cisco SD-WAN zero-day this year; Cisco confirmed limited cases where exploitation pushed configuration changes to edge devices, with no patch or workaround yet available.

incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails carrying malicious RAR archives that exploit a year-old WinRAR path-traversal flaw (CVE-2025-8088) to plant payloads in Windows Startup locations, delivering the GiftedCrook stealer and HTA-based espionage malware.
incidents.impact: Two Russia-aligned clusters harvested credentials, browser data and documents from military innovation centers, military formations and law enforcement; campaigns remained active into April-June 2026.

incidents.vector: Operators posed as women seeking romance or volunteers offering aid on Telegram, luring soldiers into installing 'SafeLoveStealer' Android spyware or entering Telegram credentials on spoofed login pages.
incidents.impact: A previously undocumented group (dubbed SiribClone) stole files, location data and Telegram sessions and could remotely activate device microphones to collect battlefield intelligence from troops near the front line.

incidents.victim: Microsoft Exchange hybrid / Exchange Online organizations
incidents.vector: 'Ghost-Sender' weakness lets attackers send email from any internal or external address against orgs using an external MX record in Exchange hybrid mode, bypassing SPF, DKIM and DMARC with a single PowerShell command.
incidents.impact: Researchers say fewer than half of exposed orgs have mitigations and Microsoft support indicated the issue (or an adjacent one) is being actively abused for spoofing, enabling convincing phishing, fraud and CEO impersonation.

incidents.victim: Check Point VPN customers (several dozen organizations)
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of a critical authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-50751, 9.3 CVSS) in Check Point Remote Access/Mobile Access VPN using the deprecated IKEv1 protocol, allowing VPN sessions without a valid password.
incidents.impact: Exploited in the wild since at least May 7 against a few dozen organizations globally; Check Point confirmed at least one case where post-exploitation activity tied to a Qilin ransomware affiliate.

incidents.vector: Social-engineering and 1-click phishing links pushing targets to external sites, plus test accounts and groups created on WhatsApp, in a campaign Meta attributed to spyware maker NSO Group despite a standing court injunction.
incidents.impact: Meta disrupted the NSO-linked activity and filed a contempt-of-court complaint; the campaign resembled Pegasus spyware infections that targeted journalists and activists in Jordan from 2019-2023.

incidents.victim: Organizations across IT, education, financial and professional services
incidents.vector: Phishing, malvertising and SEO campaigns impersonating AI brands (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Claude, DeepSeek) with payment-update and account-appeal lures leading to credential-harvesting and adversary-in-the-middle pages.
incidents.impact: Microsoft tracked campaigns sending up to 100,000 emails a day; one ChatGPT-themed wave harvested credit card data while a Claude-themed wave hit 2,000+ organizations to steal credentials and access tokens; initial access broker Storm-3075 delivered Fox Tempest-signed malware.

incidents.victim: US legal, professional and financial services firms
incidents.vector: Voice phishing and IT-helpdesk impersonation to trick staff into screen-sharing and installing remote-management tools (AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, SuperOps); in some cases actors physically entered offices posing as technicians to copy data via USB.
incidents.impact: UNC3753 (Silent Ransom / Luna Moth) hit dozens of firms Jan-May 2026, sometimes moving from initial contact to exfiltration and extortion in under an hour, stealing legal agreements, PII and tax records and demanding ransom under threat of public leak.

incidents.victim: Microsoft (Azure GitHub repositories) and downstream developers
incidents.vector: A self-propagating 'Miasma' variant of the Shai-Hulud worm abused compromised contributor credentials to poison 73 Microsoft GitHub repos and earlier the durabletask PyPI package, planting config files that execute payloads when repos are opened in AI coding tools.
incidents.impact: 73 repos (mainly Azure) were taken offline, breaking CI/CD pipelines worldwide that referenced Azure/functions-action; the credential-stealing payload targeted Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor and VS Code, harvesting tokens to seed further compromise.

incidents.victim: US military personnel in CENTCOM theater
incidents.vector: Adversary purchase and exploitation of commercially available geolocation data drawn from the digital advertising ecosystem to identify where US troops congregate and their patterns of life.
incidents.impact: CENTCOM confirmed multiple threat reports of adversaries using commercial location data to target or surveil US personnel in theater; the data is believed to have been used by Iran to help target strikes on US bases in the Middle East.

incidents.vector: Repeated network intrusions by attackers linked to foreign governments, including Chinese hackers, alleged in a whistleblower lawsuit by IBM's former VP of threat intelligence.
incidents.impact: The complaint alleges IBM and AT&T concealed multiple breaches over years from the US government and made false security assurances to win and keep federal contracts; the whistleblower says he was told to soften reports and omit details from the NSA.

incidents.vector: Attackers minted 99 million TSR tokens and dumped them on BNB Chain, crashing the token price and swapping the proceeds to stablecoins.
incidents.impact: Roughly $2.5 million was stolen, bridged to Ethereum and laundered through Tornado Cash; the platform had not addressed the incident at time of reporting.

incidents.vector: Brute-force attack against the password manager's accounts.
incidents.impact: Almost 20 encrypted password vaults were stolen; Dashlane published a post-mortem with limited technical detail on the intrusion.

incidents.victim: Obama White House and US Space Force Instagram accounts
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran actors tricked Meta's AI customer-support bot into adding an attacker email to target accounts during the password-reset flow, using a VPN with an IP near the target's hometown, then hijacked the accounts.
incidents.impact: High-value Instagram accounts including the Obama White House and the Chief Master Sergeant of the US Space Force were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian images and messages; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and data theft, with the company subsequently named on the ShinyHunters dark-web leak portal.
incidents.impact: The American telecom confirmed a security breach after appearing on the extortion group's leak site.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion and data theft attributed to the Play ransomware group, which claims to have stolen sensitive financial documents from the corporate network.
incidents.impact: The Play group is extorting the company over allegedly stolen financial records; MyPillow had not confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Use of compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to access land and real estate data.
incidents.impact: Roughly 600,000 records were stolen, including real names, cadastral information and other property details from the national registry.

incidents.victim: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with admin access to the agency's code platform created a public GitHub profile ('Private-CISA') and disabled GitHub's secret-scanning protection, publishing plaintext credentials.
incidents.impact: AWS GovCloud keys and credentials to dozens of internal CISA systems were exposed (archive created November 2025); the agency was still struggling to invalidate the leaked secrets as lawmakers demanded answers.

incidents.victim: Australian MP Zali Steggall and staff
incidents.vector: Suspected foreign-state compromise of the WhatsApp account of an Australian MP and three staffers, believed to be part of a campaign targeting Signal and WhatsApp accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: The independent MP's and staffers' messaging accounts were breached in March; the activity is unconfirmed but assessed as likely part of a Russian campaign against foreign politicians.
